 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. In just a few short years, a lot has changed for star forward Jaylen Brown . As recently as 2024, he was at the top of the basketball world with the Boston Celtics , leading them to their 18th championship alongside his talented running mate, Jayson Tatum .
 His success didn't end there, however, as Brown was named the Finals MVP for his efforts, forever cementing his place in NBA history. But when looking back on what should have been the height of his tenure in Boston, Brown explained that he never actually cared about the MVP and never expected to win it in the first place.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I think one of my highest moments is just winning a championship," said Brown in a chat with Lil Baby . "I didn't play to win no award. When they gave me the MVP, they gave me 2 MVPs, by the way, just for those, you know what I mean. But when I won, I was never expecting that. I didn't care nothing about that. It mattered way more to some people than it ever mattered to me. So when I won, you could see in my face that I was shocked. Cause it didn't change no reaction if anybody else would have won. But that don't always be the case when the shoe was on the other foot." 
 It's always been hotly debated whether Brown even deserved Finals MVP that year . With averages of 20.8 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 5.0 assists on 44.0% shooting, his numbers were fine enough, and his impact on defense was undeniable. You could also make a case for Jayson Tatum, though, who averaged 22.2 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 7.2 assists per game on 38.8% shooting from the field in the series.
 Whatever the reasoning , voters gave the nod to Jaylen, and many believe it set off a domino effect that led to his departure. By winning the Finals MVP that year, Brown experienced a massive ego boost, and he suddenly began moving with more authority on the team. Whether intentional or not, Jaylen caused a crisis in the locker room by disturbing the team's delicate internal hierarchy, all for an award he wasn't even working for.
 The result was a Celtics team that felt he no longer fit their vision, prompting urgency to make a trade that would balance the scales. At the time, the best they could do was a package involving Paul George and draft picks, but they stand by the move to this day. In fact, without Brown, the Celtics are predicted to be among the major players in the Eastern Conference this season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement For his part, Jaylen has already moved on from the past to fully commit to his new team . For the first time in his career, he won't be under Tatum's shadow, and it will be interesting to see how it impacts his game. For the 76ers ' sake, he must play like the guy who won the Finals MVP a few years back, or they might have some second thoughts about taking on his massive 5-year, $285 million contract (three years left with $183 million).
